title: chore(objectui): bump the console pin to 31971ff1e28f (one zod instance in the vendored Console), add a single-zod canary to build-console.sh, and key the release console cache on the spec zod range
body:
Fixes #21108

Clause-②: no

Moves the console pin past objectstack-ai/objectui#11353, so the vendored Console bundles one zod instance again. Adds a single-zod canary to `scripts/build-console.sh`, and keys `release.yml`'s Console dist cache on the spec's declared zod range.

## Target: `31971ff1e28f`, the minimal containing commit

`.objectui-sha` moves `e420df310f5b` -> `31971ff1e28f89cfc45f0c19bc5b05e443f28b79`. That is the merge commit of objectui#11353 itself, which closed objectui#11327. objectui `main` was `2124d0411175`, 2 commits further on, when I chose the target.

Why not `main`:
- The two later commits are objectui#11293 (standalone `object-kanban` / `object-calendar` honour `page` navigation through the host's record navigator) and objectui#11165 (a docs example and its test). Neither is needed by this card.
- objectui#11293 rewrites `plugin-kanban/src/index.tsx` and `plugin-calendar/src/index.tsx`. Nine asserting pin-citation anchors in `packages/spec/src` read those two files. Taking it would turn this pin's citation re-measure into a navigation-claim change outside this card.
- The procedure (`docs/releases-maintenance.md`) says the target is decided in the objectstack issue. The card's unlock criterion is "a commit that contains objectui#11353". The minimal containing commit meets it and drags in the least.

Containment was measured on a private full clone of objectui (`rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = false):

| question | command | exit |
|---|---|---|
| pin is the objectui#11353 merge | `gh api …/pulls/11353` answers `merged: true`, `merge_commit_sha: 31971ff1e28f…` | — |
| pin is on objectui `main` | `merge-base --is-ancestor 31971ff1e28f origin/main` | 0 |
| old pin is inside the new range | `--is-ancestor e420df310f5b 31971ff1e28f` | 0 |
| negative: new pin is not inside the old one | `--is-ancestor 31971ff1e28f e420df310f5b` | 1 |
| control for that negative (deeper commit, same target) | `--is-ancestor db11afd4967c e420df310f5b` | 0 |
| objectui#11293 is NOT in this pin | `--is-ancestor 2124d0411175 31971ff1e28f` | 1 |
| control for that negative | `--is-ancestor e420df310f5b 31971ff1e28f` | 0 |

The range `e420df310f5b..31971ff1e28f` is 44 commits.

## What changed

- **`.objectui-sha` and `.changeset/console-31971ff1e28f.md`.** Written by `scripts/bump-objectui.sh 31971ff1e28f --no-commit` against the private clone, so the shared shallow `../objectui` was never deepened. The range has 56 releasing changesets, 12 declared breaking, and 3 commits carry no changeset.
  - objectui#11353, the fix this bump exists for, is one of those 3. So I added one lead sentence naming it; the digest would otherwise list it only under "declared nowhere".
  - The bump script's `adr-0087: TODO` placeholder is answered `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. It is worded after the maintainer's ruling on the previous bump (#20949) and fitted to this diff, and it names all 12 upstream entries. Three of them mirror ObjectStack keys that are already retired and registered here: `ui/ChartConfig:aria`, `ui/Page:assignedProfiles` and `ui/Action:aria`. The `object-form` / `object-map` / `object-gantt` / `object-chart` entries move objectui's validator onto the `properties` bag that the spec rows already declare. `showFilters` was never an ObjectStack key on `object-grid`. Please confirm this disposition; see the open question in the report on #21108.
- **`sdui.manifest.json` + `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json`.** Produced by `node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs` over the tree `build-console.sh` built at the pin: 107 components, `@object-ui/core` 17.6.0. Eleven components changed their published inputs: `object-form`, `object-kanban`, `object-calendar`, `object-gantt`, `object-timeline`, `object-map`, `record:quick_actions`, `element:text`, `element:definition-list`, `element:repeater` and `action:button`.
- **`packages/sdui-parser/objectui-lockstep.json`.** Re-recorded with `pnpm gen:sdui-lockstep` against the pin's own checkout: 214 grammar lines, 25 codes, containment predicate `76c18fb95d1f`. `check:sdui-lockstep` exits 0 with no port owed.
- **`scripts/build-console.sh`: the single-zod canary.** Details in the next section.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`: the Console dist key.** Details below.
- **The 49 asserting pin citations in `packages/spec/src`.** Re-measured at the new pin (section below). This also regenerates `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` (`gen:migration-registry`) and `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx` (`check:generated --fix`, the one artifact it proved stale), and adds `.changeset/objectui-pin-citations-31971ff1e28f.md` (`@objectstack/spec` patch). The `FormField.span` describe and six migration-entry descriptions name the pin, so the text change publishes.
- **`origin/main` merged once (`19cbfeba7d`).** No file overlaps this diff, and no generated artifact moved.

## The single-zod canary

It sits beside the existing bundle canary.
- It counts zod version literals across `packages/console/dist/assets/*.js`. Each zod 4 instance carries one version object (the `version` export of `zod/v4/core/versions`), minified as `{major:4,minor:6,patch:5}`.
- It requires **exactly one** occurrence. It refuses two different versions (the shipped defect), one version found twice (two instances), and zero (a blind matcher, since the console always bundles zod).
- The same function runs standalone as `scripts/build-console.sh --check-single-zod ASSETS_DIR`, which builds and writes nothing. That standalone mode is how both directions below were measured.

| fixture | result |
|---|---|
| the real dist this PR's build produced at `31971ff1e28f` (2450 `assets/*.js`) | exit 0: `exactly one zod version literal {major:4,minor:6,patch:5} in vendor-objectstack-UrN_Az-7.js` |
| the real `db11afd4967c` dist (the published two-zod split) | exit 1: `2 different zod versions` — `vendor-objectstack-CfLtdaY1.js:{major:4,minor:6,patch:1}`, `vendor-zod-CHLW1iCr.js:{major:4,minor:4,patch:3}` |
| the new dist plus one chunk carrying `{major:4,minor:4,patch:3}` | exit 1, two different versions |
| the new dist plus a second `{major:4,minor:6,patch:5}` chunk | exit 1: `2 copies of ONE zod version literal` |
| the new dist with its one literal rewritten (`major` -> `MAJOR`; `grep -o` count 1 -> 0 before, 0 -> 1 after) | exit 1: the blind-matcher refusal |
| no argument | exit 2, usage |

The fixtures are copies in a scratch directory. No tracked file was mutated.

## `release.yml`: the key carries the spec's declared zod range, not the whole `package.json`

The card suggested `hashFiles('packages/spec/package.json')`. I went with a narrower input:
- A new step reads `dependencies.zod` out of `packages/spec/package.json`. It fails rather than emitting an empty or `undefined` range.
- The restore, the `CONSOLE_DIST_CACHE_KEY` env and the save step all spell the same key, with `-zod-RANGE` appended (today `-zod-^4.6.1`).

Why not hash the whole file: its `version` field moves on every Version Packages merge, and that merge is the push that drives the publish lane. Hashing it would make every publish a cache miss and a cold console rebuild. The comment above the key records that design as deliberate. The declared range is the input the build actually judges: objectui#11353's parity assertion refuses a console zod outside it.

`release.yml` is not a governed surface. `GOVERNED_SURFACES` in `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` lists `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`. No workflow was run or dispatched.

## Pin-citation re-measure

Each record was handled the same way:
- Its anchors were mapped through the `e420df310f5b..31971ff1e28f` diff of each cited file and re-read at the new pin.
- Block hashes (`git hash-object`) and corpus counts (`git grep -o -F` over the tracked tree, 9912 files) were taken again with the method each record names. The method reproduces every `e420df310` count exactly at the old pin: 9800 files, `objectstack` 15352, `@objectstack/spec` 6024, `timeout` 1293.
- Earlier hops stay as history.
- `check:objectui-pin-citations --verify-anchors`, run against the pin's checkout, reports 49 asserting citations matching `31971ff1e`, and 7 anchor content assertions verified.

Records whose CLAIMS moved, not only their numbers. These want a human read:
- **`object-calendar` `navigation`.** objectui#8652 declared the key on `ObjectCalendarSchema`. That removes the one `as any` cast objectui#8651 had left: the ledger comment `1008-1025` is replaced by a declaration note, and the read `1026` -> `1018` now says `schema.navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer' }`.
- **`object-kanban` `navigation`.** The read is unchanged. It now compiles through a declared `ObjectKanbanSchema.navigation` member rather than `BaseSchema`'s index signature.
- **`object-timeline`.** objectui#8654 declared `navigation`. The read lost its cast (`753-756` -> `793-796`), and both registrations gained a `navigation` input. The `schema.*` read set is unchanged, because `navigation` was already read and is already on this row.
- **`action:button`.** objectui#11168 slice 2 makes the `size` input publish the five values the row declares. The `inputs` range grew `414-551` -> `414-559`.
- **`record:quick_actions`.** objectui#10224 rewrote the fail-closed docblock: the bar is replaced by the notice, not hidden. The cited gate lines moved by 6 with their text byte-identical.
- **`object-tree` optionality count.** By the record's own method, `plugin-map/src/index.tsx` now reads 4 `ElementDataSourceGate` hits, not 3. objectui#10859 batch 5 added a comment naming the gate, while the wiring is still three lines. The record now says so.
- **Wrong when written.** The `object-timeline` data door's start/end-binding anchor `621-622` began one line early, on the `rawData.map` head, at `e420df310` too. It is re-pointed to `657-658` and the record says why.

No key, default, enum member or export moves.

## Acceptance at the new pin

**Build.** `scripts/build-console.sh` ran at `31971ff1e28f` with this tree's client and spec injected, under the shared verify lock: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- The single-zod canary passed (above). `assert-console-spec-injection` passed: 21 of 21 injected-only descriptions are present and all 8 published-only ones are absent.
- The dist is 63032 KB.
- Environment, not a product change: objectui's `jsdom` requires Node `^22.22.2` under engine-strict, and this container's Node is 22.22.0. A verified Node 22.22.2 was prepended to `PATH` for the console build only.
- The build ran before the manifest regeneration, as the procedure orders it. So that local dist ships the previous manifest bytes, and the build itself prints the re-run step. CI's Console Pin Gate builds fresh.

**Boot.** `pnpm dev -- --fresh --ui --no-watch -p 41633` started the showcase with its own ephemeral DB and the seeded admin. `check:console-sha` reads `objectui@31971ff1e28f`. I drove it in headless Chromium (`/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`) from `localhost`:
- **Studio "New package (writable base)"** (`/_console/studio`): the dialog renders **Display name (`name`)**, **Package ID (`id`)** and **Object namespace (`namespace`)**, plus Version, Type and Description.
  - I filled `Zod Probe` / `com.acme.zodprobe` / `zodprobe` and clicked Create package. The request was **`POST /api/v1/packages` -> 201**.
  - The Studio opened `/_console/studio/com.acme.zodprobe/data`. `GET /api/v1/packages/com.acme.zodprobe` answers 200 with `writable: true`.
- **Dashboard inspector** (`/_console/apps/showcase_app/metadata/dashboard/showcase_ops_dashboard`): the spec-derived form renders Columns, Gap, Refresh Interval Seconds, Header, Show Title, Show Description and Actions. "Spec schema unavailable" appears 0 times.
- **Report inspector** (`…/metadata/report/showcase_task_overview`): Label, Report type, Description and Blocks render, with 0 "Spec schema unavailable".
- **Control for that absence:** the string is in the shipped bundle (`i18n-D40RWXZZ.js`, 3 occurrences), so 0 on screen is a reading, not a missing probe.
- **Errors:** 0 page errors and 0 console errors across the drive.
- **Non-2xx:**
  - `401 GET /api/v1/auth/get-session` before sign-in.
  - `404 GET /api/v1/usage/storage`, as at the previous pin.
  - `501 GET /api/v1/ai/usage`, with no AI provider configured.
  - `404 GET /api/v1/meta/{dashboard,report}/NAME?state=draft`, the no-draft probe of a code-loaded item.
- **Teardown:** only the 7 PIDs I recorded were stopped. The port is free, and the `--fresh` tempdir went with the process.

## Gates and tests, at head `19cbfeba7d`

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 151 commands, all run sequentially with exit codes captured before any pipe.
  - 150 exit 0.
  - `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` hit my 900 s runner timeout under contention (exit 124). Re-run alone with no timeout, it passed: exit 0, `dispatch-gates self-test: 1976 cases pass`, battery 1096.7 s.
  - `dispatch-gates --ran` reconciliation: `151 derived, 151 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
  - Highlights: `check:objectui-pin-citations` 49 matching, `check-sdui-manifest` intact at the live pin, `check:sdui-lockstep` OK, `check:console-sha`, `check:console-injection`, `check-adr-0087-registration` (2 declaring changesets, each with a disposition), `check:generated` (15 of 15 current), `check:docs` (227 in sync), `check:migration-registry`, `check:bash32-floor` (32 shell files), `check:nul-bytes`, `check-ci-filter-parity` and `check:published-files`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: 591 files, 17368 passed and 1 todo, exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0.
- NOT MEASURED, by CI only: the Console Pin Gate job's own steps and the workspace type-check lanes. The local equivalent of the Console Pin Gate is the build above.

## Acceptance notes

- `scripts/check-console-injection.mjs`'s header still says release.yml's key "hashes the pin and the build script". That sentence is now incomplete, because the key also carries the spec's zod range. The file is outside this card's file surface. It is a comment, and nothing reads it.
- objectui#11353 landed with no objectui changeset, so objectui's own CHANGELOG does not mention the zod fix. The console changeset here names it.
